assumptions.reason: User explicitly requested DDR3-800 speed grade
User specified '2kb', interpreted as x16 device width which provides 2KB page size
Performance goal does not mention reliability; ECC off to avoid extra lane and latency overhead
Only 1 rank is supported today; defaulting to 1

rationale: The user is requesting to finalize the specification with all previously established parameters: DDR3-800 speed grade, 4Gb density, x16 device width, and the performance-oriented microarchitecture settings (fr_fcfs scheduler, open_page policy, 32-entry command queue, 16-deep lookahead, 4 byte lanes, no ECC, 1 rank).

legend.isolated: Change the value freely. No RTL structure/port/width change -- at most a constant, a CSR reset value, or a backend hint. Safe to sweep.
legend.regen_local: A few modules' parameters (widths, depths) change and those modules regenerate, but port names and the cross-module interface stay stable.
legend.structural: Bus/address widths, geometry or port lists change; ripples across most modules and the cross-phase lint must re-pass.
legend.unsupported: Current RTL agents do not implement this axis; the compiler rejects it.

isolated.effect: Backend synthesis hint only. Frontend RTL agents ignore it.
Backend synthesis hint only. Frontend RTL agents ignore it.
Backend timing-closure goal. No RTL change as long as it stays >= the controller clock the speed grade needs.
Refresh policy constant + REFRESH_CONFIG reset value. Fits the existing 4-bit CSR field; no port change.
Refresh policy constant + REFRESH_CONFIG reset value. Existing 4-bit field.
BIST pattern / address range. Existing CSR fields, no port change.
Behavioural selectors in refresh_ctrl / data_path; no interface change.
Counter compare value in init_fsm. No port change while it fits the counter width.
Counter compare value in calibration / scheduler.

regen_local.effect: Drives queue_index_bits -> cmd_queue + scheduler parameter widths. Port names stable. Must be a power of 2.
Drives lookahead_index_bits -> scheduler. Port names stable.
wb_port / data_path read-return FIFO depth. Local parameter.
wb_port / data_path write FIFO depth. Local parameter.
scheduler behaviour + CTRL_CONFIG.sched_policy reset bit (bit already exists). No port change.
scheduler / bank_tracker behaviour + CTRL_CONFIG.row_policy reset bit. No port change.
refresh_ctrl behaviour + CTRL_CONFIG.self_ref_mode reset field. No port change.
addr_decoder bit-slicing logic changes; its port list stays the same.
Adds/removes pipeline registers -> latency_model + data_path. Interface stable.

structural.effect: Every timing constant, tCK, all clock periods, CL/CWL, mode registers, TIMING_* CSR reset values, latency model. Touches timing / init_fsm / config_regs / scheduler / bank_tracker / data_path.
Changes row_bits -> address_width_bits -> addr_decoder, bank_tracker, every module carrying a row-address port, and the BIST address range. tRFC also changes.
Changes channel_data_width -> data_path packing, phy_interface, addr_decoder, host burst sizing, capacity/address width.
x8 vs x16 changes page size -> column_bits, row_bits, channel width. Ripples like density.
BL4 vs BL8 changes tCCD, data-beat count, data_path packing and the latency model.
wb_port bus width, wb_sel width, data_path pack_mode, and every host-facing port.
wishbone_classic vs _pipelined changes the wb_port protocol FSM and stall semantics.
ECC on consumes a byte lane and widens the data_path with SEC-DED logic; changes channel data width and ERROR_STATUS use.

unsupported.effect: ranks > 1: current RTL agents assume a single rank (bank_tracker / addr_decoder have no rank dimension, no ODT / rank-switch handling).
num_ports > 1: only a single Wishbone host port is implemented (no arbiter instancing in wb_port).
